acceptance.given: A supported package-validation route policy is supplied, including candidate policies that omit the VDD route or the Acceptance route.

oracle.expected: The validator rejects every policy whose supported route set lacks the VDD route or the Acceptance route, preserving both as irreducible required routes.
forbidden: A policy without the VDD route is accepted.
A policy without the Acceptance route is accepted.
The minimum supported route set is reduced.
oracle.observable: The package-policy validator returns a rejection result and identifies the missing irreducible route.

acceptance.then: The VDD and Acceptance routes remain irreducible and required.
acceptance.when: Run the Toolchain package-policy validator against route sets containing both required routes and against route sets with either required route removed; evaluate the validation result and diagnostic.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Use the existing validator test selector to supply a route policy missing the VDD route or Acceptance route and assert that policy validation fails closed.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Enforce the minimum supported package-validation route policy so neither the VDD nor Acceptance route can be removed; validation rejects either omission.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve existing validation behavior for policies containing both required routes; rollback only the irreducible-route enforcement without changing persisted state or schemas.

slice_hint.state_transition: A candidate route policy transitions from unvalidated to rejected when either irreducible route is absent; policies retaining both remain eligible for validation.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Validation terminates with failure for every supported route set lacking VDD or Acceptance, and no such policy is accepted.

acceptance.given: A valid target package is supplied with a validator capability substituted for the repository-trusted capability, while all non-substitution inputs remain valid.

oracle.expected: The validator-capability selection rejects the substituted capability with a nonzero result and emits no trusted validation receipt.
forbidden: Proceeding with a substituted validator capability.
Treating an undeclared validator as the trusted capability.
A trusted pass receipt for the substituted capability.
oracle.observable: The targeted pytest case invokes the replay entrypoint with the substitution fixture and observes the nonzero rejection plus absence of a trusted result.

acceptance.then: The substituted validator capability is rejected without a trusted result.
acceptance.when: When a validator capability other than the required capability is supplied or selected.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Execute the existing replay unit selector with an isolated substituted-capability fixture and require the entrypoint to fail closed.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Bind validator selection to the repository-trusted capability identity and reject an invocation whose supplied capability resolves to an undeclared substitute before validation can produce a trusted result.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No persisted state or receipt-schema migration is introduced; rollback restores the prior capability-selection behavior in the replay entrypoint.

slice_hint.state_transition: A supplied or selected undeclared validator capability transitions from candidate selection to fail-closed rejection, with no trusted validation result.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The targeted unit selector demonstrates that substituting the validator capability yields a nonzero rejection and no trusted validation receipt.

acceptance.given: A candidate and a validator capability with its source, content, semantic dependencies, compatibility, support policy, and scope are available for evaluation.

oracle.expected: An independent verification establishes candidate-external trust from the bound validator capability and complete dependency closure rather than another verification's conclusion.
forbidden: Trust inferred solely from another verification
oracle.observable: The validator evaluation result exposes an independently verified candidate-external trust binding.

acceptance.when: The validator evaluation selector evaluates the candidate and its bound validator capability.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Supply candidate-controlled or incomplete trust bindings and observe the independent trust check reject them.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Independently evaluate candidate-external validator trust against bound source, content, dependency, compatibility, policy, and scope identities.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Untrusted or candidate-controlled bindings fail closed and do not become trust authority.

slice_hint.state_transition: Candidate trust unverified -> independently verified candidate-external trust or rejected evaluation.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The evaluation independently binds candidate-external trust and rejects omitted, inherited-only, candidate-controlled, or incomplete trust verification.

acceptance.given: An applicable Consumer has completed enable, disable, and behavioral rollback through its applicable route sequence.

oracle.expected: The applicable Consumer invokes the current approved Candidate Route through its real call surface and exposes the resulting re-enable execution.
oracle.observable: A real Consumer call surface records or exposes successful re-enable execution.

acceptance.then: Re-enable has been executed by the applicable Consumer through a real call surface.
acceptance.when: After disable and behavioral rollback, re-enable is exercised for the applicable Consumer.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Use a skip or simulated-call condition and observe that re-enable cannot be accepted without a real Consumer Candidate-Route call.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Require each applicable Consumer to re-enable by invoking the current approved Candidate Route through its real call surface and capture that call's result.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Re-enable remains a Candidate-Route invocation after the prior disable and rollback sequence; configuration-only switching is insufficient.

slice_hint.state_transition: Applicable Consumer after behavioral rollback -> real Candidate-Route re-enable call recorded.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Every applicable Consumer's re-enable transition invokes the real Candidate Route and exposes its current execution result.
